name: Management consultancies

problems.words: We write proposals for weeks and can't tell which ones are still alive
quick_ideas: Go through every proposal sent in the last three months once and mark it live, lost or unknown, so you see the real pipeline
Give each live proposal a named owner, so someone is responsible for the next contact.

workzap_build.text: a pipeline tracker with stage, owner and next action date for every proposal, reminding the owner automatically when a follow-up is due.

problems.free_stops: the stages and follow-up timings for your type of client are set out in the solution document.

problems.words: Our win rate is low but we don't know why we lose
quick_ideas: Ask your last few lost clients one polite question about why, so you get real reasons
Note those reasons in one place, so patterns become visible.

workzap_build.text: loss reasons captured every time a bid closes, with a regular view of wins and losses by service line and client type.

problems.free_stops: how loss reasons are captured and grouped is designed in the solution document.

problems.words: Clients keep adding work without paying for it
quick_ideas: List the extra requests on your largest live engagement, so you see how far it has drifted
Raise that list with the client once, so the conversation about a change happens.

workzap_build.text: a scope change log per engagement where each request is recorded, approved and flagged for billing.

problems.free_stops: the approval and billing steps are kept for the solution document.

problems.words: Fixed-fee projects run over by months
quick_ideas: Compare days used against days planned once for each live engagement, so the overruns are on the table
Review the worst one with its lead, so you catch it earlier next time.

workzap_build.text: an engagement tracker showing effort used against plan every week, with alerts when an engagement starts to slip.

problems.free_stops: how effort is tracked and when alerts fire are worked out in the solution document.

problems.words: Some consultants are overloaded and others are on the bench
quick_ideas: Put every consultant's bookings for the next eight weeks on one page, so gaps and overloads show
Use it once to rebalance one overloaded person, so the benefit is felt straight away.

workzap_build.text: a resource planner showing who is booked where week by week, with bench time and overloads visible to the partners every day.

problems.free_stops: how bookings are entered and kept current is designed in the solution document.

problems.words: Milestone invoices go out late because sign-off is stuck
quick_ideas: List every deliverable that has gone to a client without a sign-off, so you know what is holding invoices
Ask for each sign-off in writing once, so the request is on record.

workzap_build.text: a milestone billing trigger where the invoice is drafted as soon as a deliverable is signed off, with sign-off chasers and receivables ageing.

problems.free_stops: the trigger points and chaser timings are set out in the solution document.

problems.words: Government clients pay six months late
quick_ideas: Check once what paperwork each slow client needs with an invoice, so nothing is sent back for a missing document
Make one list of overdue invoices by client, so collections has a clear order.

workzap_build.text: receivables per client with ageing, document checklists per invoice and scheduled reminders.

problems.free_stops: the reminder flow and checklists per client type are kept for the solution document.

problems.words: Every proposal is written from scratch and good frameworks sit on someone's laptop
quick_ideas: Collect your best recent proposals and case write-ups into one shared folder, so the team can find them
Tag them by service line once, so reuse is easy.

workzap_build.text: a proposal library of past proposals, CVs and case write-ups tagged by service line, searchable by the whole team.

problems.free_stops: the structure and tagging of the library are designed in the solution document.

problems.words: Timesheets are filled in at month-end from memory
quick_ideas: Ask the team to note time daily for one week, so you can compare it with the usual month-end version
Share utilisation per person once, so people see why it matters.

workzap_build.text: a weekly timesheet linked to engagements with daily nudges, showing utilisation per consultant as it happens instead of after month-end.

problems.free_stops: the timesheet format and nudge timings are set out in the solution document.

problems.words: Associates invoice us late and argue over days worked
quick_ideas: Confirm days worked with each associate in writing at the end of this week, so there is an agreed record
Note the agreed rate for each one in a single list, so invoices can be checked quickly.

workzap_build.text: an associate register with availability, agreed rates and days confirmed weekly, matched automatically against their invoices.

problems.free_stops: how confirmations and matching work is kept for the solution document.

never_say: Any strategy, financial, legal or tax advice for the consultancy or its clients.
Anything involving inducements, kickbacks, bid-rigging or obtaining competitors' bids.
That win rates or margins will improve by any amount.
Requests for client names, tender references or associates' personal or tax details.

sample_reply.person: We send a lot of proposals and honestly have no idea which ones are still live. What would you suggest?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this can be sorted, and you can start this week. 1) Go through the last three months of proposals once and mark each live, lost or unknown, so the real pipeline is visible. 2) Give every live one a named owner, so somebody is responsible for the next contact. Workzap can do this automatically for you: a pipeline tracker with stages, owners and follow-up reminders, plus loss reasons recorded every time. Would you like me to put together a solution document and quote for you? You're free to say no.
